name: Brentwood
seo_title: Christmas Events for Kids in Brentwood, CA 2026
seo_desc: Kids' Christmas in Brentwood, CA: the Holiday Parade, the Winter Market with free train rides, the City Park tree lighting and Christmas on the Farm.
lede: Brentwood celebrates Christmas downtown and on the farm: a Chamber of Commerce parade of lighted floats, a city Winter Market and tree lighting in City Park, and a windmill lighting at the historical society's museum grounds.
celebrates: The season starts with the Brentwood Chamber of Commerce Holiday Parade, an evening of illuminated floats and community groups that runs from First Street through downtown to Brentwood Boulevard at Oak Street. The City of Brentwood Parks and Recreation Department then hosts the Brentwood Winter Market downtown, with vendors, games and crafts, carolers and free holiday train rides, and lights the Christmas tree in City Park. Decorated Deck the Park trees fill City Park. Out on Sellers Avenue, the East Contra Costa Historical Society holds Christmas on the Farm with Santa photos and the Lighting of the Windmill at dusk.
lastyear: In 2025 the Brentwood Chamber of Commerce held its 43rd Annual Holiday Parade on Saturday, November 29, with the theme Holiday Toyland. The parade began at 5 pm with illuminated floats and community groups moving through downtown. Afterward the City of Brentwood held its Community Sing-Along and Tree Lighting Ceremony in City Park, led by Mayor Meyer, with free hot cocoa, cookies and holiday crafts for all ages. In 2026 the city moves its tree lighting to the Winter Market weekend.
facts: Brentwood began in the 1870s on land that had been Rancho Los Meganos, a name meaning sand dunes in Spanish. Dr. John Marsh, the first American to live in East Contra Costa County, bought the rancho in 1837 and built the John Marsh Stone House. The popular belief is that Brentwood was named for Marsh's ancestral home in Essex County, England. The town's first building was J. P. Carey's blacksmith shop in 1874, and residents voted to incorporate on January 15, 1948.
trains: Trains helped put Brentwood on the map. The San Pablo and Tulare Railroad added Brentwood as a stopping point in 1878, the same year the first post office opened, and by the end of the 1920s the H. P. Garin Company was shipping almost 800 railroad carloads of fruits and vegetables across the country. Today BART's eastern end is Antioch station on Highway 4 at Hillcrest Avenue, opened in 2018, and Amtrak stops at the Antioch-Pittsburg station on I Street. At the Winter Market, children can ride free holiday trains on Second Street.

kidfact: Brentwood, California, is probably named after a town in England called Brentwood, where the family of John Marsh came from. Marsh built a big stone house nearby that still stands.
faq: When is the Brentwood Holiday Parade?

The Brentwood Chamber of Commerce holds its Holiday Parade on a Saturday evening in late November. In 2025 the 43rd parade, themed Holiday Toyland, started at 5 pm on November 29, running from First Street through downtown to Brentwood Boulevard at Oak Street. The 2026 parade is the 44th, with the theme Brentwood Express.
Where is the Brentwood Christmas tree?

The city's Christmas tree is in City Park in Downtown Brentwood. In 2025 it was lit after the Holiday Parade with a sing-along led by Mayor Meyer. In 2026 the City of Brentwood lights it during the Brentwood Winter Market, with performances by East County Performing Arts Center groups and a special appearance by Santa.
Are there train rides at Christmas in Brentwood?

Yes. The City of Brentwood's Winter Market includes free holiday train rides on Second Street on the Sunday of the market weekend. Brentwood also has railroad history: the San Pablo and Tulare Railroad made the town a stop in 1878, and farms here shipped fruit and vegetables across the country by rail.
What is Christmas on the Farm?

It is the East Contra Costa Historical Society's holiday celebration on the first Sunday in December at its museum grounds on Sellers Avenue. The society lists games, music, family activities, food and craft vendors, photos with Santa and ornament making for kids, ending with the Lighting of the Windmill at dusk. Admission is free.
